title: Exact Gaussian-elimination cost: tightening n³ to (n³ − n)/3

problemStatement.formal: Forward Gaussian elimination of an n×n system costs gaussExactOps n = ∑_{j<n}(j²+j) multiplications+divisions, with 3·gaussExactOps n + n = n³, i.e. gaussExactOps n = (n³ − n)/3.
problemStatement.plain: The parent Cramer-vs-Gauss entry bounds Gaussian elimination by the loose n³ multiplication model. This entry proves the exact leading count is (n³ − n)/3 — the classic 'n³/3 flops' — tightening the model by a factor of ~3 while keeping every comparison conclusion.
whyMatters: Pins down the exact leading constant (1/3) behind the textbook flop count for Gaussian elimination / LU factorization.
Upgrades the parent's loose, axiomatized n³ model to a fully kernel-checked exact closed form (no native_decide, axiom-free).

proven: gaussExactOps n = ∑_{j<n}(j²+j) — exact per-step model (j divisions + j² multiplications at the step with j rows below the pivot).
gaussExactOps_closed: 3·gaussExactOps n + n = n³ (subtraction-free closed form, induction + ring in the ℕ semiring).
gaussExactOps_eq_div: gaussExactOps n = (n³ − n)/3 (textbook n³/3 flop count).
gaussExactOps_le_cube and gaussExactOps_lt_cube: ≤ n³ always, strict for n ≥ 2 (the factor-3 tightening is genuine).
gaussExact_beats_cramer: the tighter model still beats Cramer's rule for n ≥ 4, a fortiori from the parent gauss_beats_cramer.
open: Additions/subtractions (~n³/3), the full ~2n³/3 forward-elimination flop total, and the complete multiplication+division solve count (factorization + RHS + back-substitution, with solve_overhead_quadratic: it exceeds the factorization count by exactly n²) are now formalized. Remaining: the back-substitution additions/subtractions for the complete-solve flop total.
Generalizing to block / Strassen-style elimination where the leading constant changes.
knownResults.goal: Replace the loose n³ Gaussian-elimination model with the exact (n³ − n)/3 count and confirm the Cramer-vs-Gauss verdict is preserved.

currentState.focus: Exact (n³ − n)/3 operation count formalized and proved axiom-free.

insights: Stating the closed form subtraction-free as 3·ops + n = n³ keeps the induction in the ℕ semiring so plain `ring` closes the successor step; the (n³ − n)/3 division form is then a one-line corollary. linear_combination would not work here because ℕ is not a ring.
A tighter cost for the comparison winner can never overturn the comparison: gaussExactOps n ≤ n³ = gaussMuls n lets gaussExact_beats_cramer inherit the parent's n ≥ 4 verdict for free.
omega abstracts n³ and the Finset sum as opaque non-negative atoms linked only by the linear closed-form hypothesis, which suffices for both the ≤ and strict-< bounds without any cubic reasoning.

Deriving the concrete small-n counts (2,8,20,40) from the closed form via omega instead of native_decide keeps the file free of Lean.ofReduceBool — verified/original rather than the parent's axiomatized status.

Complete-solve full flop count = (4n³+9n²−7n)/6 ~ 2n³/3, the textbook "flops to solve a dense linear system". Crossover vs loose n³ model is EXACTLY n=4. GOTCHA: solveMulsDivs≤solveFlops must be proved STRUCTURALLY (unfold to gaussExactOps/Subs/gaussSum atoms) not via closed forms — omega treats n³,n² as independent atoms.
